# Issue #69 contrib-node compatibility PoC

## Run identity and constraints

- Evidence branch: `poc/contrib-node-compatibility`
- Baseline checkout: `f2a57e2dba235e3f661328c20fdc5bbad70fb57e`
- Baseline Node-RED: repository fork `5.0.7`; runtime package pins upstream Node-RED packages `5.0.7`.
- Baseline Temporal SDK: runtime package pins `@temporalio/*` `1.24.0`.
- Baseline `npm test` first attempt: **BLOCKED before tests** because `node_modules/marked/marked.min.js` was absent. Ran `npm ci` using the unchanged lockfile, then reran `npm test`: **PASS, 3,436 passing / 61 pending**, coverage Statements 65.86%, Branches 59.34%, Functions 65.4%, Lines 65.96%. No production or dependency-manifest changes were made.
- Upstream zero-diff guard: PASS (no output from the required `git diff --stat upstream/main -- ...` command).
- Issue #69 comments at research start: empty (`gh api repos/tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal/issues/69/comments` returned `[]`).
- This file records a predeclared corpus. Package versions below are exact npm registry `npm view <package> version` results observed before installation/testing, not evidence of compatibility.
- Packages are to be installed only into disposable user directories outside the repository. Existing listening processes are not owned by this PoC and will not be stopped or reused.

### Excluded/reference case (not in the new corpus)

FlowFuse Dashboard 2.0 evidence from issue #64 is reused by reference only, without repeating its experiment. Closed issue #64's outcome comment records `@flowfuse/node-red-dashboard@1.31.0`, PASS after generic `runtime.httpNode` hosting, real Temporal executions in both directions, and runner restart/browser reconnect. This resident web/socket service and its widget messages are not counted as a newly tested package/node here.

### Research results gathered before corpus testing

- Node-RED official documentation, via Context7 `/node-red/node-red.github.io`, describes the modern input callback as `(msg, send, done)` and says `done` must be called when handling completes; legacy compatibility examples include fallbacks to `node.send`/`node.error`.
- Node-RED official documentation recommends installing a node module from the Node-RED user directory and starting Node-RED with an explicit custom user directory.
- Context7 `/martin-doyle/node-red-contrib-aedes` documents `node-red-contrib-aedes` as a broker node with configurable MQTT listener, optional WebSocket/TLS and persistence options. This is a resident service/config candidate, not an ordinary message Activity.
- Flow Library documentation for `node-red-contrib-email@0.3.1` documents SMTP transport config (`host`, `port`, `secure`, auth mode) and `email-send` output fields. The installed exact-version source uses async `(msg, send, done)` and calls `done()` after `sendMail` completion.
- Context7 `/nodemailer/smtp-server` documents a real local SMTP server `onData(stream, session, callback)` sink; the PoC binds it to loopback only. `smtp-server@3.19.17` was installed `--no-save --no-package-lock` into the disposable userDir as test-service tooling, not as a Node-RED dependency.
- Flow Library docs for `node-red-contrib-buffer-parser@3.2.2` list `buffer-maker` as the Buffer-producing node. Installed source inspection found its one-argument input handler at `buffer-maker.js:600`.
- Registry metadata lookup confirmed the exact versions listed above before testing. `node-red-contrib-sqlite` is unpublished; `node-red-node-sqlite@2.0.1` was selected as its explicit replacement, not silently substituted after a test outcome.
- Targeted package research for this continuation: Flow Library `node-red-contrib-cron-plus` page (3.2.0) documents static/dynamic schedules and schedule persistence; `node-red-node-sqlite` page (2.0.1) documents `sqlitedb`, `msg.topic` queries and `msg.payload` results; `node-red-contrib-fs-ops` page (1.6.0) describes filesystem operation nodes and pass-on-success/error behavior; `node-red-contrib-queue-gate` page (1.5.5) describes open/closed/queueing commands and context-backed state. Context7 `/node-red/node-red-nodes` also returned the SQLite config/query contract and parameter usage. The matching package pages are `https://flows.nodered.org/node/node-red-contrib-cron-plus`, `https://flows.nodered.org/node/node-red-node-sqlite`, `https://flows.nodered.org/node/node-red-contrib-fs-ops`, and `https://flows.nodered.org/node/node-red-contrib-queue-gate`.
- The PostgreSQL 0.6.1 npm page documents a PostgreSQL node and sample config. Targeted lookup of `https://flows.nodered.org/node/node-red-contrib-postgres` returned 404; npm metadata/readme was available at `https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-red-contrib-postgres`. Context7 resolution did not identify the contrib package as a library, so the exact package/runtime behavior was established by source and stock-runtime execution instead of relying on a guessed documentation match.

## Direct real-runner evidence

Disposable userDir: `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir`; packages installed with one `npm install --prefix /tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir --no-audit --no-fund <package>@<version> ...` command (15 packages, 207 packages added). No repository dependency manifest was modified.

The selected runner was a fresh combined worker against a separately started Temporal dev server, not the pre-existing processes on ports 7233/8233/1881/1882. For the email/buffer continuation, the isolated Temporal process used port 17233, runner Admin API 19181, and SMTP sink 1025:

```bash
temporal server start-dev --ip 127.0.0.1 --port 17233 --ui-port 18233 --headless --db-filename /tmp/nrt-issue-69-temporal.sqlite
node packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/bin/node-red-temporal worker --role combined --flow packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/poc/flows.moment-smoke.json --user-dir /tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir --address 127.0.0.1:17233 --workflow-task-queue issue69-wf --activity-task-queue issue69-act --admin-port 19181 --admin-host 127.0.0.1
```

Ports 17233, 18233, 19181 and 11883 were checked free before startup. The moment flow entered through the real Node-RED Inject source, scheduled `executeNode` Activities for `moment` and `debug`, and completed with `lastNode: issue69-debug`. Temporal event 7 contained a successful `moment` Activity result with `payload: "2024-01-02T03:04:05.000Z"`, `destinationId: issue69-debug`, and ordinary JSON settings. Restarting the runner with the same userDir/flow generated a second completed Workflow, proving ordinary node reinstall/load and execution after process restart. The exact first and restarted Workflow IDs are in the matrix.

For the legacy case, the same runner command used `poc/flows.string-legacy-smoke.json`. Temporal Workflow `ingress:5e1eb2fc-1152-4897-82a0-60558bcaf76a` had an `executeNode` Activity scheduled and completed with `error.code` represented as `NODE_ERROR`, message beginning `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE`, and a captured send to `issue69-legacy-debug` carrying the trimmed payload `temporal legacy`. Workflow failure was non-retryable. This is a real contrib package execution and confirms the expected explicit boundary, not successful Activity compatibility.

For the resident service case, `poc/flows.aedes-source-smoke.json` instantiated the contrib `aedes broker` config/service node on port 11883 and Node-RED's core `mqtt in` source. A real MQTT client published to `issue69/source`; Temporal Workflow `ingress:779ce408-5a4f-470f-b169-d7ac50fea125` completed the captured core `change` and `debug` Activities with the expected payload. After stopping only the owned runner process and restarting with the same userDir/flow, the Aedes listener returned on 11883 and another real publish started completed Workflow `ingress:2ddc09d4-ac52-4540-844b-01848fc4ad4d`. This classifies the contrib broker as `CONFIG_SERVICE`; the autonomous source node in this flow was Node-RED core's `mqtt in`, not a contrib source.

The PostgreSQL package load warning is exact: the Temporal runner logged `[node-red-contrib-postgres/PostgreSql] Error: Cannot find module 'undefined/red/red'` with require stack `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir/node_modules/node-red-contrib-postgres/postgres.js`. Exact package source line 17 requires `process.env.NODE_RED_HOME + "/red/red"`. To compare stock parity, I independently ran the stock Node-RED 5.0.7 CLI in safe mode against the same existing userDir. The command was:

```bash
timeout --signal=TERM 12s node packages/node_modules/node-red/red.js --userDir /tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir --port 19480 --safe
```

Port 19480 was verified free first. Stock startup logged:

```text
[node-red-contrib-postgres/PostgreSql] Error: Cannot find module '<repo>/packages/node_modules/node-red/red/red'
Require stack:
- /tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir/node_modules/node-red-contrib-postgres/postgres.js
```

The CLI had set `NODE_RED_HOME`, but this source-tree layout still has no such `red/red` module. Thus the load failure is reproduced under stock Node-RED and is not evidence of a Temporal-specific package-loading defect. No PostgreSQL service or credentials were configured, and no database operation was attempted. The bounded safe-mode command exited after 12 seconds; it created `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir/settings.js`, and that pre-existing userDir was not cleaned or deleted.

### A2 local side-effect and A7 restart: contrib email

The service helper is `poc/local-smtp-sink.js`, using `smtp-server@3.19.17` installed only in `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir` with `--no-save --no-package-lock`. It bound exclusively to `127.0.0.1:1025`, accepted unauthenticated SMTP on loopback, and logged accepted message envelopes/bodies to `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-smtp.log`. The runner flow used `node-red-contrib-email@0.3.1`'s `email-transport` config and `email-send` Activity; sender/recipient use the reserved `.test` domain and no external email was sent.

- First send: Workflow `ingress:aaa27e16-9c74-4bd9-aebf-52073cd38806` completed. Its `email-send` `executeNode` Activity completed with accepted recipient `receiver@example.test`, SMTP response `250 OK: message queued`, and routed `msg.payload` containing `accepted`, `envelope`, `messageId`, and response. The sink log captured body `issue69-local-smtp-side-effect` from remote `127.0.0.1`.
- Restart check: after stopping only the owned runner and restarting with the same userDir/flow, Workflow `ingress:fcf2126d-c833-496d-a070-85eea1893176` completed and its message was separately captured by the same local sink. This establishes A2 and a useful A7 side-effect case; it does not establish exactly-once behavior if an Activity is retried.

### A6 Buffer producer

Flow `poc/flows.buffer-maker-smoke.json` executes the predeclared real `node-red-contrib-buffer-parser@3.2.2` `buffer-maker` type with a four-byte ASCII `B640` value. Temporal Workflow `ingress:97887a7b-1d4d-49a5-aed4-a5827a8fc2e5` scheduled the `executeNode` Activity, captured its send to the debug node, then failed non-retryably with `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE`. In the raw decoded `ActivityTaskCompleted` result JSON, the captured `msg.payload` was `{ "type": "Buffer", "data": [66,54,52,48] }`. This proves the generated Buffer reached Temporal's activity error-result details with that JSON representation; it does not establish a successful Activity-to-next-Activity Buffer path, and the node's primary classification remains `LEGACY_NO_COMPLETION`.

### Continuation: cron-plus, SQLite, fs-ops and queue-gate

The four checked-in JSON flows `poc/flows.cron-plus-smoke.json`, `poc/flows.sqlite-smoke.json`, `poc/flows.fs-ops-smoke.json`, and `poc/flows.queue-gate-smoke.json` were parsed before use. All tests used the existing `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir`; no package or repository manifest was changed. The dedicated Temporal dev server listened on 127.0.0.1:27233 (PID 338544, database `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-followup-temporal.sqlite`), the combined runner used task queues `issue69-followup-wf`/`issue69-followup-act`, Admin API port 29181, and HTTP ingress port 29281. `ss -ltnp` showed these selected ports free before service startup. Existing processes on 7233, 1880, 1881 and 1882 were not used or stopped.

Cron-plus 3.2.0 was deployed with a configured UTC `*/5 * * * * *` schedule emitting `cron-plus-3.2.0`. While the real combined runner was live it started four completed autonomous-source Workflows: `ingress:5e86b9cb-a211-4e4a-8831-c94b262ea33b`, `ingress:c2c65445-db95-45ed-8345-8a5634931325`, `ingress:3bae2d65-188b-46d1-b31a-622d61ddc700`, and `ingress:8bc3758c-ba52-4bea-bb82-b8f833e3483f`. Each history has 11 events and a completed downstream `executeNode` Activity for `issue69-cron-debug`; the inspected event-1 Workflow input retained the schedule payload, topic and `msg.cronplus` status/config metadata. `node-red-contrib-cron-plus@3.2.0` is therefore directly classified `RESIDENT_SOURCE` for this configured schedule. No runner-restart or schedule-state persistence claim is made.

SQLite was started as an actual `sqlite` node with `sqlitedb` configured for `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir/issue69-smoke.sqlite`. The CLI start command supplied the tested SQL via `msg.topic` (`SELECT 69 AS issue_number, sqlite_version() AS version`) and Workflow `node-red-temporal-1791352895963` scheduled/completed its `executeNode` Activity, then failed non-retryably with `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE`; the completed Activity's captured error had `sends: []`. The file existed afterward but was zero bytes, and neither successful DB-open logging nor a query result was observed. This supports the node's `LEGACY_NO_COMPLETION` classification, not successful SQLite operation. A separate initial HTTP ingress attempt had supplied JSON body fields expecting them at the message root; the documented ingress contract wraps the body under `msg.payload`, so that attempt failed with `msg.topic : the query is not defined as a string` and is excluded from the package verdict.

The filesystem flow ran `fs-ops-access` against the known existing `/tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir/package.json` and enabled its real access check. Temporal Workflow `node-red-temporal-1791352943084` scheduled/completed `executeNode` and failed non-retryably with `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE`. The exact callback contract prevents claiming a successful downstream handoff; the row is classified `LEGACY_NO_COMPLETION`, with no filesystem-output/restart claim.

The queue-gate flow constructed `q-gate@1.5.5` in open state with in-memory context and sent a real input payload. Temporal Workflow `node-red-temporal-1791352977902` scheduled/completed `executeNode` and failed non-retryably with `LEGACY_NODE_NO_DONE`. No queue persistence, state-transition, or restart behavior is claimed; the observed row classification is `LEGACY_NO_COMPLETION` under the current Activity boundary.

For remaining service availability, `command -v influxd` and `command -v mbserver` returned no executable. The available local Docker image inventory contained PostgreSQL (`postgres:16`) but no recognizable InfluxDB or Modbus server image; PostgreSQL itself remained untestable because the package failed loading identically under stock Node-RED. No secrets or Telegram credentials were inspected.

Reproduction commands (run from repository root; each runner invocation used the corresponding flow in place of `<flow>` and was stopped by its captured PID before the next flow):

```bash
temporal server start-dev --ip 127.0.0.1 --port 27233 --ui-port 28233 --headless --db-filename /tmp/nrt-issue-69-followup-temporal.sqlite
node packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/bin/node-red-temporal worker --role combined --flow <flow> --user-dir /tmp/nrt-issue-69-userdir --address 127.0.0.1:27233 --workflow-task-queue issue69-followup-wf --activity-task-queue issue69-followup-act --admin-port 29181 --admin-host 127.0.0.1 --http-ingress-port 29281 --http-ingress-host 127.0.0.1
node packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/bin/node-red-temporal start --flow packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/poc/flows.sqlite-smoke.json --start-node issue69-sqlite --input '{"topic":"SELECT 69 AS issue_number, sqlite_version() AS version"}' --address 127.0.0.1:27233 --workflow-task-queue issue69-followup-wf --activity-task-queue issue69-followup-act
node packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/bin/node-red-temporal start --flow packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/poc/flows.fs-ops-smoke.json --start-node issue69-fs-access --input '{}' --address 127.0.0.1:27233 --workflow-task-queue issue69-followup-wf --activity-task-queue issue69-followup-act
node packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/bin/node-red-temporal start --flow packages/node_modules/@tbrandenburg/node-red-temporal-runtime/poc/flows.queue-gate-smoke.json --start-node issue69-qgate --input '{"payload":"queue-gate-smoke"}' --address 127.0.0.1:27233 --workflow-task-queue issue69-followup-wf --activity-task-queue issue69-followup-act
```

### Directly tested, reused, and not tested
